messages:
OpsBot: INCIDENT detected: cont-batch tail-latency spike in us-west-2 (streaming path). p95 -> 420ms, p99 -> 4.2s, a few streaming sessions stalled >30s. Auto-page: @alex oncall.

Alex: on it. seeing a cluster-wide increase in cont-batch tail. diving into batcher logs + scheduler metrics.

Alex: quick perf snapshot:
- sustained batch sizes up to 128 on hetero sequences
- queue depth spiked, packing inefficiencies, KV cache thrash on some hosts
- many requests pinned to single busy worker leading to queuing

Maya: @alex thanks — initial thought: mixed sequence lengths + aggressive max_batch_size causing amplification. can we temp reduce max_batch_size and enable seq-aware packing?

Alex: agree. rolling a low-risk mitigation: reduce max_batch_size from 128 -> 32 for streaming-executors in us-west-2 on the cont-batch pool. also flip on preemptive_streaming_shed=true (30s).

Prateek: +1. how are we going to do that safely? need a canary then wider roll.

Alex: will canary on two hosts (uw2-batch-12/13) then widen if tail improves. running command now:
```
infractl rollout --pool contbatch-usw2 --set max_batch_size=32 --canary 2 --timeout 300s
```

Sofia: heads-up, customer-impact: we've got 3 high-value streaming customers in us-west-2 showing retries and elevated error budget usage. engineering-sre on call is notified. Customer success ready for possible contact.

PagerDuty: Paging update: on-call acked by Alex at 4123500006. escalation path intact.

Maya: also recommend adjusting scheduler fairness weights to prefer streaming lanes for next 15m. quick curl to control plane:
```
curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/v1/scheduler/weights -d '{"contbatch": {"streaming_weight": 1.5, "batch_weight": 1.0}}'
```

Alex: canary finished. applying to remainder of contbatch-usw2 pool. starting in 60s.

OpsBot: rollout started (job id r-41235-01). health checks enabled.

Prateek: monitoring p95/p99 and streaming stall count. pulling kv-eviction logs — looks like some workers hit kv_cache_evictions/sec spikes coincident with tail spikes. suggests prefix cache churn.

Maya: if eviction is the culprit, lowering cache size isn't great. alternative: increase per-request kv_hint for long-lived streams so they pin KV entries. short term: raise kv_cache_capacity on canary hosts by 25%.

Alex: applied kv_cache_capacity bump on canary hosts. will include metric delta in 1m.

Sofia: contacting CS with a short blurb: "We're investigating streaming stalls in us-west-2; temporary mitigation in progress (config rollouts). We expect reduced stalls within 10-20 minutes. Will follow up"

Alex: metrics update @4123500240: p95 dropped to 210ms, p99 dropped to 1.1s, streaming-stalls count down 85% on canaries. Going to continue rollout.

Prateek: good signal. widening rollout to remaining hosts (batch-safe window).

OpsBot: rollout progressed to 80% (r-41235-01). No failed hosts.

Maya: one more tuning: enable seqlen_bucket_threshold=64 so very short requests pack separately from long ones. reduces padding amplification.

Alex: applied seqlen_bucket_threshold on all contbatch-usw2.

Sofia: customers updated: CS notified 3 affected customers with mitigation note, monitoring for residual errors.

Prateek: monitoring shows steady state now. p95 190ms, p99 850ms, streaming stalls returned to baseline.

Alex: handoff incoming — @prateek you're next oncall. summary for shift: cause = mixed sequence lengths + oversized max_batch_size causing queue amplification + KV cache churn. mitigations applied: reduced max_batch_size -> 32, seqlen bucketing, increased kv_cache_capacity on contentious hosts, scheduler fairness weight tweak.

Prateek: taking over. thx @alex. I'll keep the rollbacks ready and watch the dashboards.

PagerDuty: Handoff recorded at 4123500402.

Sofia: creating follow-up ticket and postmortem stub: INF-41235 (cont-batch tail latency due to mixed seqlen packing). tagging eng-runtime, eng-sre, eng-ml for longer-term fixes (adaptive batching, better seqlen-aware scheduler heuristics).

Alex: closing page for now. will attach logs and canary diffs to INF-41235. great teamwork :thumbsup:

Prateek: final check-in at 4123500420: all clear in us-west-2, watch windows for next 2 hours. leaving note: prioritize a test harness to simulate heavy mixed-seqlen streaming traffic.
